# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04**
**Member: Emerson Hayes | Member ID: W807153430**
**Reference Number: POC-9668BA39E4-60948**
**Procedure: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881)**
**Governing Policy: Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316)** — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

Dear Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which was denied in the notice dated 2026-08-04 on the grounds that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's own criteria

The Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet lists the specific non-operative treatments the plan looks for. Among them, the guideline names:

> "oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection"

and

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment:"

My records show that I completed several of these specific treatments before surgery was requested:

- **Physical therapy:** 24 supervised visits over 14 weeks (2026-03-30 to 2026-07-06), focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Pharmacologic treatment:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection:** administered 2026-04-23, giving only 2 weeks of partial relief.

These are not a partial or incidental effort — they reflect a sustained, supervised course covering multiple categories the plan's own tip sheet identifies as evidence of conservative care.

The tip sheet also states:

> "The guidelines should be reviewed for additional requirements including duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria and for the complete listing of other procedures not included below."

My records address each of these elements:

- **Duration of symptoms:** 12 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical examination:** positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Radiographic/imaging findings:** MRI dated 2026-05-24 showing a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.

I also want to note that my MRI showed a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 1, with articular cartilage preserved. The plan's own guideline states:

> "MRI should not be the primary tool used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

My surgery is not being requested because of arthritic changes — it is being requested because of a displaced meniscal tear causing mechanical locking and giving way, which the MRI directly documents. The KL grading scale in the guideline is described as a measure of arthritic change, not of meniscal tear pathology, so I do not believe my low KL grade is a basis to deny a procedure addressed to a different finding — a locked, displaced meniscal tear that limits my ability to squat, kneel, or do more than walk on level ground.

I recognize that the excerpts I have been given from the tip sheet describe specific non-operative requirements for lateral release and for debridement chondroplasty of patellofemoral chondrosis, and that the guideline itself notes there may be additional or different listed requirements for other procedures not included in these excerpts. My meniscus tear and mechanical locking do not appear to be either of those two conditions, and I have not been provided the specific listed criteria that apply to a displaced meniscal tear. I am asking the plan to review my case against whatever specific criteria do apply to this procedure and confirm how my documented 14-week course of physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID use, and corticosteroid injection are weighed against those requirements.

## What I am asking

I am asking Harvard Pilgrim Health Care to reconsider this denial and approve the requested knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), in light of the conservative treatment I have already completed and the mechanical symptoms documented in my chart.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-01-31**. I am submitting it by phone at 1-888-333-4742 (Member Services) and to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed.

Please let me know if any additional records or forms are needed to complete this appeal.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Emerson Hayes
Member ID: W807153430
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
